svg.title: The oesophageal cancer treatment map: stage × histology → road
svg.desc: Schematic treatment map for oesophageal cancer: stage by histology points to a road. Taiwan SCC at diagnosis: stages III plus IV 77.3% (registry plus NHI database 2008–2014, ages 40–79, n=7,763; SCC 96.6%, adenocarcinoma 3.4%). Five squamous boxes: box 1, cT1a mucosal disease, endoscopic resection; JES CQ6 says that for pT1a-MM with lymphovascular invasion or pT1b, additional surgery or chemoradiotherapy are both supported. Box 2, cStage I: oesophagectomy or definitive chemoradiotherapy with close follow-up and salvage, both weak JES recommendations; a matched Taiwan study found no difference in clinical stage I. Box 3, resectable cStage II–III, three roads: preoperative chemoradiotherapy plus surgery (CROSS 10-year overall survival 38% vs 25%; NEOCRTEC5010 SCC 5-year 59.9% vs 49.1%), preoperative chemotherapy plus surgery (Japanese DCF, JES strong recommendation A; JCOG1109 3-year 72.1% vs 62.6%), and definitive chemoradiotherapy with or without salvage surgery (JCOG0909 single arm, 5-year overall survival 64.5%, oesophagus preserved 54.9%; ESMO footnote: preferred for unwilling or unfit patients and cervical tumours); ASCO 2020 writes 'or', ESMO 2025 'equally effective'; actual Taiwan SCC distribution: definitive chemoradiotherapy 54%, preoperative chemoradiotherapy plus surgery 26%, surgery alone 20%. Box 4, cT4b: definitive chemoradiotherapy (JES CQ12 weak, consensus 100%); surgery if it becomes resectable has weak evidence. Box 5, metastatic: systemic therapy, palliation of swallowing, trials and palliative care in parallel; postoperative nivolumab only for residual tumour in the specimen. Adenocarcinoma column: perioperative FLOT plus surgery, ESMO [I, A]; ESOPEC 3-year overall survival 57.4% vs 50.7% with CROSS, HR 0.70; preoperative chemoradiotherapy only if unfit for FLOT [I, C].

g.text: STAGE × HISTOLOGY → ROAD
The oesophageal cancer
treatment map: stage × histology
→ road
Squamous cell carcinoma runs down the five boxes; adenocarcinoma takes a
different road (FLOT) in the locally advanced box. Each box carries the
guideline grade; every number carries its trial name.
Where you land is decided by imaging, biopsy and the multidisciplinary
meeting — this map is for asking, in clinic, 'which box am I in?'
Stage at diagnosis, Taiwan SCC: stages III + IV together 77.3%
(Cancer Registry + NHI database 2008–2014, ages 40–79, n=7,763; SCC
96.6%, adenocarcinoma 3.4% of these two types)
Squamous cell carcinoma (over 90% in Taiwan)
Box 1 | cT1a, mucosa
Endoscopic resection (ESD/EMR) can deal with it
JES 2022 CQ6: if the specimen shows pT1a-MM with lymphovascular
invasion, or pT1b, additional oesophagectomy or chemoradiotherapy are
both supported and neither can be singled out (consensus 89.3%,
evidence C).
→ 'Can endoscopy alone deal with an early lesion?'
Box 2 | cStage I (T1bN0)
Oesophagectomy, or organ-preserving definitive
chemoradiotherapy with close follow-up and salvage
JES CQ5: both carry only a weak recommendation (consensus 92.3%, C).
A matched Taiwan registry study (cT1–3 SCC, n=4,931) found no
survival difference between the two in clinical stage I.
→ 'What surgery removes' · 'Why a higher radiation dose is not better'
Box 3 | cStage II–III, resectable
Three roads the guidelines recognise — ASCO 2020 writes
'or', ESMO 2025 writes 'equally effective with regard to
OS'
Preoperative chemoradiotherapy + surgery
CROSS (n=366, 75% adenocarcinoma): 10-year OS 38% vs 25% with
surgery alone; SCC subgroup HR 0.48.
NEOCRTEC5010 (SCC, n=451): 5-year OS 59.9% vs 49.1%.
ESMO 2025 [I, A]
Preoperative chemotherapy + surgery (the Japanese
standard)
JES CQ8, strong recommendation A: preoperative DCF triplet
chemotherapy.
JCOG1109: 3-year OS 72.1% with DCF vs 62.6% with CF (HR 0.68).
Same box, different mainstream by country
Definitive chemoradiotherapy (± salvage surgery)
JCOG0909 (cStage II/III SCC, n=94, single arm): 5-year OS 64.5%,
oesophagus preserved in 54.9%.
ESMO 2025 footnote: preferred for patients unwilling or unfit for
surgery, and for cervical tumours.
JES CQ7: surgery first = weak (C)
Where Taiwan SCC patients actually stand (registry 2008–2016, cT1b–4 N0/+
Definitive CRT 54%
Definitive CRT 54% Preop CRT + surgery 26% Surgery alone 20%
Box 4 | cT4b, airway or great vessel
Not resected first: definitive chemoradiotherapy
JES CQ12: weak recommendation for definitive chemoradiotherapy
(consensus 100%, C); CQ14: if it becomes resectable after
chemoradiotherapy, surgery has only weak evidence (consensus 89.3%,
→ 'The tests that decide operability' · 'When to come back the same day'
Box 5 | Metastatic
Systemic therapy, palliation of swallowing, trials and
palliative care — in parallel, not in sequence
Immunotherapy plus chemotherapy is stratified by PD-L1 (see the
immunotherapy article). Postoperative nivolumab is limited to residual
vital tumour in the resection specimen (ESMO 2025 footnote g; JES
CQ9, strong recommendation A).
→ 'Who does immunotherapy actually help?' · 'After recurrence or metastasis'
Adenocarcinoma | locally advanced, resectable
Adenocarcinoma takes another road
Resectable locally advanced adenocarcinoma: perioperative FLOT
chemotherapy + surgery [I, A] (ESMO 2025 interim update).
ESOPEC (Germany, n=438): 3-year OS 57.4% with FLOT vs 50.7% with
CROSS, HR 0.70; 90-day postoperative mortality 3.1% vs 5.6%.
Preoperative chemoradiotherapy only if unfit for FLOT [I, C].
Neo-AEGIS (mostly older ECF/EOX) was a draw.
→ 'Squamous and adenocarcinoma are two different diseases'
Boxes move: deeper than expected after ESD → box 2; metastasis found on PET after
chemoradiotherapy → box 5; a T4 tumour shrinking on re-evaluation → box 3. The map is
drawn once; other articles do not redraw it.
Schematic, redrawn from the JES 2022 guideline, the ESMO 2025 interim update, the ASCO
2020 guideline, CROSS (Eyck 2021), NEOCRTEC5010 (Yang 2021), JCOG0909, ESOPEC
(Hoeppner 2025) and Taiwan Cancer Registry studies (Chen HY 2022, Chen HS 2022, Chang
2022) | cohorts, stages and endpoints differ between trials — numbers in different boxes
are not directly comparable | where you land is for the multidisciplinary team to judge
